newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, June 13 - We had trimmed our final estimate on CPO production in May by 4,000 tonnes to 780,000 tonnes. This represents an increase of 47,000 tonnes or 6.4 percent over April. With the exception of three large producers which posted double-digit increases, the majority recorded gains of 5-7 percent in output. The five-week dry spell in the country had been broken since last week when good rains with coverage of up to 50 percent fell in most crop areas in the late afternoon/evenings. We thus expect a pickup in production from next week onward.

In tandem with the cut in production, the final estimate on palm oil stocks at end-May is lowered by 5,000 tonnes to 740,000 tonnes, or about 40,000 tonnes more than month earlier. For the second consecutive month, output of PK/PKO exceeded offtake. This resulted in a further buildup in stocks. End-May stocks of PK/PKO are estimated at around 150,000 tonnes as against 133,400 tonnes a month earlier and 124,000 tonnes a year ago, oil basis. We are maintaining our estimate of palm oil exports of 635,000 tonnes in May and 610,000 tonnes in April.

The modest increase in shipments reflected chiefly growth in offtake by India and Pakistan. Exports to China were little changed at an estimated 115,000 tonnes while shipments to Europe were down by around 15,000 tonnes. At this moment we still do not expect exports this month to be better than May.

After losing 82-56 ringgit in the first six trading days of this month, CPO futures regained some lost ground in the last three days with prices gaining 15-12 ringgit. The bulk of the gains in both the futures and cash markets was attributed to short-covering activities rather than to new export sales.

The rather heavy and early CPO tenders of 280 lots (7,000 tonnes) between June 6-11 had the effect of forcing spot month futures to as big a discount as 15 ringgit against the one month forward contract on June 10. The spread narrowed to 10 ringgit yesterday. In the absence of positive leads on the export front, traders are not inclined to initiate new long positions. Most of them trimmed their positions in recent days as reflected in the downtrend in the open position for CPO futures - 7,949 contracts as of June 13 versus 8,486 on June 2.

Short-term weather outlook in U.S. soybean/corn crop land meanwhile remained favourable with the USDA projecting a soybean harvest of 2.6 billion bushels, up 9.2 percent from 2.36 billion bushels in 1996/97. The Indian monsoon also continued to improve, especially in the southwest.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
